hook: After mating, male mice's dopamine release drops and takes about a week to recover, tracking their drive.
summary: Deep-brain imaging in the medial preoptic area showed tonic dopamine falling after mating and returning over several days. Reduced firing of dopamine neurons explains the first day or two, while a slower loss and recovery of the neurons' ability to make dopamine explains the rest of the week. This is in male mice only.
title: Slow-timescale regulation of dopamine release governs recovery of a motivational drive over days.
